source_text:
θεϊκῶς, ὁμοούσιον δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν τὸν αὐτὸν ἀνθρωπίνως. τοῖς οὕτω φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις
ἀναστρέψει Χριστὸς τοῦ καθ' ἑαυτὸν μυστηρίου τὴν γνῶσιν.
βʹ. Ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ τιμωμένη τε καὶ ἁγιαζομένη· ὅτι
γὰρ τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι, οὔτ' ἂν ἐδεήθη βαπτίσματος, οὔτε μὴν τοῦ Ἁγίου
Πνεύματος μετασχεῖν, μάλιστα μὲν ἀρκέσει πρὸς πληροφορίαν τὸ αὐτὸν εἶναι τοῦ
Πνεύματος χορηγόν.
thought_title: Christ reveals the mystery to those who think rightly
orientation: Cyril is closing his argument, stating that Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery to those who have chosen to think rightly about him.
pass_a_gloss: Divinely, consubstantial [he is] and with us the same [one] humanly. To those having chosen to think thus, Christ will reveal of the mystery concerning himself the knowledge. For the nature of man, the [one] in Christ, was being honored and sanctified; for as far as [it] has come to being, neither would he have needed baptism, nor indeed to share in the Holy Spirit; most of all it will suffice for full assurance [that] he himself is the giver of the Spirit.

choices.why: The verb here means to turn back or return, but in this context it carries the sense of disclosing or making known; 'reveal' fits the mystery language.

choices.term: τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι
choices.english: as far as his own being is concerned
choices.why: The phrase means 'as far as it pertains to being' or 'with regard to existence'; the rendering keeps the limiting force of τό γε ἧκον.
rejected: as far as it has come to be
in respect of coming into being

choices.why: The noun denotes complete confidence or certainty; 'full assurance' captures the sense of settled conviction.
The glossary requires 'giver' for χορηγός, the one who supplies or bestows the Spirit.

pass_b_english: Divinely, consubstantial, and also to us the same humanly. To those who think thus Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery. For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified. For as far as his own being is concerned, he would not have needed baptism, nor indeed to share in the Holy Spirit. Most of all it will suffice for full assurance that he himself is the giver of the Spirit.

problems.quote: Divinely, consubstantial with the Father; and with us, the same one humanly.
problems.source_quote: θεϊκῶς, ὁμοούσιον δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν τὸν αὐτὸν ἀνθρωπίνως.
problems.why: Source does not mention “with the Father”; it says simply “Divinely, consubstantial, and also to us the same humanly.”
problems.fix: Divinely, consubstantial, and also to us the same humanly.
problems.ruling: ὁμοούσιον δὲ lacks 'with the Father'; δὲ is 'but/and', no Father mentioned.

problems.quote: To those chosen to think thus Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery.
problems.source_quote: τοῖς οὕτω φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις ἀναστρέψει Χριστὸς τοῦ καθ' ἑαυτὸν μυστηρίου τὴν γνῶσιν.
problems.why: Source says “to those who think thus, the deserted (abandoned) …”, not “chosen”.
problems.fix: To those who think thus, Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery.

edits.old: Divinely, consubstantial with the Father; and with us, the same one humanly.
edits.new: Divinely, consubstantial, and also to us the same humanly.

edits.old: To those chosen to think thus Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery.
edits.new: To those who think thus Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery.

fixed: Source: "θεϊκῶς, ὁμοούσιον δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν τὸν αὐτὸν ἀνθρωπίνως." The English added "with the Father"; removed it and adjusted to match the source.
Source: "τοῖς οὕτω φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις" means "to those who have chosen to think thus"; the English "chosen" was not in the source, so removed it.

last_rejected.quote: For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified
last_rejected.source_quote: ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ τιμωμένη τε καὶ ἁγιαζομένη
last_rejected.why: The Greek emphasizes 'the human nature' (ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις) with double article, specific and emphatic; 'the humanity' loses the technical precision and the article's force.
last_rejected.fix: For the human nature in Christ was being honored and sanctified.
last_rejected.ruling: English conveys 'human nature' as 'the humanity'; meaning preserved, article emphasis is stylistic, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: To those who think thus Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery.
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῖς οὕτω φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις ἀναστρέψει Χριστὸς τοῦ καθ' ἑαυτὸν μυστηρίου τὴν γνῶσιν.
last_rejected.why: The phrase "ᾑρημένοις" (having been set free) is omitted, losing a descriptive clause about the audience.
last_rejected.fix: To those who think thus, who have been set free, Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery.
last_rejected.ruling: ᾑρημένοις is middle voice of αἱρέομαι='having chosen,' not passive 'set free.' 'Think thus' captures sense adequately.
